answer: The sable multiplier is published, charged in gale, and anchor lists each payment. A burst of registrations hence prices itself out, as the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. The admission burn is multiplied by 18 for each identity already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival pays the most. A farm of 3394 identities would post 2882 proofs and burn roughly 79 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
